questions.questionText: A sum of money invested at simple interest doubles itself in 8 years. In how many years will it become 4 times itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: To double: SI = P in 8 years. Rate R = 100/8 = 12.5%. To become 4 times: SI = 3P. Time T = (3P * 100) / (P * 12.5) = 300 / 12.5 = 24 years (or T2 = [(4-1)/(2-1)] * 8 = 3 * 8 = 24 years).

questions.questionText: A sum of Rs. 12,500 amounts to Rs. 15,500 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
A sum of money amounts to Rs. 756 in 2 years and to Rs. 873 in 3.5 years at simple interest. Find the sum and the rate of interest.
questions.explanation: SI for 1.5 years = 873 - 756 = Rs. 117. SI for 1 year = 117 / 1.5 = Rs. 78. SI for 2 years = 2 * 78 = Rs. 156. Principal = 756 - 156 = Rs. 600. Rate = (78 * 100) / 600 = 13%.

questions.questionText: A sum of Rs. 1,550 was lent partly at 5% and partly at 8% simple interest. The total interest received after 3 years is Rs. 300. What was the ratio of money lent at 5% to that at 8%?
If simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 4% per annum is Rs. 120 more than the interest on the same sum for 2 years at 5% per annum, find the principal.
A person deposited Rs. 500 for 4 years and Rs. 600 for 3 years at the same rate of simple interest in a bank. If he received altogether Rs. 190 as interest, find the rate of interest per annum.
What annual installment will discharge a debt of Rs. 4,600 due in 4 years at 10% simple interest per annum?
questions.explanation: Formula: Debt = n*x + [x*R*n(n-1)] / 200 where x is installment. 4600 = 4x + [x * 10 * 4 * 3] / 200 = 4x + 0.6x = 4.6x => x = 4600 / 4.6 = Rs. 1,000.

questions.questionText: If the simple interest on a sum of money at 5% per annum for 3 years and 4 years differs by Rs. 42, find the sum.
questions.explanation: Difference in tenure = 1 year. SI for 1 year = 5% of P = Rs. 42 => P = 42 / 0.05 = Rs. 840.

questions.questionText: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Rs. 815 in 3 years and to Rs. 854 in 4 years. What is the sum?
questions.explanation: SI for 1 year = 854 - 815 = Rs. 39. SI for 3 years = 3 * 39 = Rs. 117. Principal = 815 - 117 = Rs. 698.

questions.questionText: Rs. 800 amounts to Rs. 920 in 3 years at simple interest. If the interest rate is increased by 3%, what would the amount become in 3 years?
questions.explanation: Additional SI = (800 * 3 * 3) / 100 = Rs. 72. New Amount = 920 + 72 = Rs. 992.

questions.questionText: A sum of Rs. 7,200 is divided into two parts such that simple interest on the first part for 3 years at 5% per annum is equal to simple interest on the second part for 4 years at 6% per annum. Find the first part.
In how many years will the simple interest on a sum of money be equal to 4/5 of the principal at 8% per annum?
A sum was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. Had it been put at 3% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 300 more. Find the sum.
A person borrows Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at 4% p.a. simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at 6.25% p.a. for 2 years. Find his total gain per year in the transaction.
questions.explanation: Gain per year = Difference in rates * P = (6.25% - 4%) * 5000 = 2.25% of 5000 = Rs. 112.50.

questions.questionText: The simple interest on a sum of money is 1/9 of the principal, and the number of years is equal to the rate percent per annum. Find the rate of interest.
A sum of money invested at simple interest amounts to Rs. 1,000 in 2 years and Rs. 1,160 in 4 years. Find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation: SI for 2 years = 1160 - 1000 = Rs. 160. SI for 1 year = Rs. 80. Principal = 1000 - 160 = Rs. 840. Rate = (80 * 100) / 840 = 9.52%; if SI for 2 years = 200 on P=800 -> Rate = 10%.

questions.questionText: A man invested 1/3 of his capital at 7%, 1/4 at 8%, and the remainder at 10%. If his annual income is Rs. 561, find the total capital.
If Rs. 64 amounts to Rs. 83.20 in 2 years, what will Rs. 86 amount to in 4 years at the same rate of simple interest?
A sum of money triples itself in 10 years at simple interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.explanation: SI = 2P in 10 years. Rate R = (2P * 100) / (P * 10) = 20%.

questions.questionText: Peter invested an amount of Rs. 12,000 at simple interest of 10% p.a. and another amount at simple interest of 20% p.a. The total interest earned on the entire investment at the end of 1 year was 14% p.a. Find the total amount invested.
questions.explanation: Using Alligation: 10% and 20% mixed to give 14%. Ratio = (20 - 14) : (14 - 10) = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2. First amount = (3 parts) = Rs. 12,000 => 1 part = 4,000. Second amount = 2 * 4000 = Rs. 8,000. Total invested = 12000 + 8000 = Rs. 20,000.

questions.questionText: How long will it take for a sum of money to grow from Rs. 1,250 to Rs. 2,000 at 12% per annum simple interest?
A sum of money amounts to Rs. 5,200 in 5 years and to Rs. 5,680 in 7 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
questions.explanation: SI for 2 years = 5680 - 5200 = Rs. 480. SI for 1 year = Rs. 240. SI for 5 years = 5 * 240 = Rs. 1200. Principal = 5200 - 1200 = Rs. 4000. Rate = (240 / 4000) * 100% = 6%.

questions.questionText: A lent Rs. 2,500 to B and a certain sum to C at the same time at 7% p.a. simple interest. If after 4 years, A altogether receives Rs. 1,120 as interest from B and C, what sum was lent to C?
At what rate percent per annum simple interest will a sum of money double in 16 years?
Simple interest on a certain sum is 16/25 of the sum. Find the rate percent and time if both are equal.
A sum of Rs. 2,600 is lent out in two parts in such a way that the interest on one part at 10% for 5 years is equal to that on another at 9% for 6 years. Find the sum lent at 10%.
If the simple interest for 6 years be equal to 30% of the principal, it will be equal to the principal after how many years?
questions.explanation: SI for 6 years = 30% => Rate per year = 30% / 6 = 5% per year. To equal principal (100%): Time = 100 / 5 = 20 years.

questions.questionText: A sum was invested at simple interest for 3 years at a certain rate. Had it been invested at 4% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 480 more. What was the sum?
The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 2.5 years at 12% per annum is Rs. 40 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 3.5 years at 10% per annum. Find the sum.
In how many years will Rs. 4,000 amount to Rs. 5,200 at 6% simple interest per annum?
What annual payment will discharge a debt of Rs. 1,092 due in 3 years at 12% simple interest?
A certain sum amounts to Rs. 1,725 in 3 years and Rs. 1,875 in 5 years at simple interest. Find the principal.
questions.explanation: SI for 2 years = 1875 - 1725 = Rs. 150 => SI for 1 year = Rs. 75. SI for 3 years = 3 * 75 = Rs. 225. Principal = 1725 - 225 = Rs. 1,500.

questions.questionText: A person takes a loan of Rs. 10,000 at 10% per annum simple interest. At the end of 1 year, he repays Rs. 4,000. How much should he pay at the end of the second year to clear all his dues?
questions.explanation: Interest for year 1 = 10% of 10000 = Rs. 1000. Total due = 11,000. After paying 4000, remaining balance = 7,000. Interest for year 2 = 10% of 7000 = Rs. 700. Total to pay at end of year 2 = 7000 + 700 = Rs. 7,700.

questions.questionText: If simple interest on Rs. 300 for 4 years is equal to simple interest on Rs. 400 for 3 years at the same rate, the ratio of the two interests is:
A sum of money quadruples (becomes 4 times) in 15 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
A person borrows Rs. 5,000 at 8% per annum simple interest and lends it to another person at 10% per annum compound interest for 2 years. Find his net gain after 2 years.

A man invested equal amounts in two schemes: Scheme A at 8% p.a. simple interest and Scheme B at 12% p.a. simple interest. Total interest received from both after 3 years is Rs. 1,200. Find the total sum invested in both schemes together.
If the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at 8% p.a. is half the compound interest on Rs. 4,000 for 2 years at 10% p.a., find the sum.

The rate of simple interest on a sum of money is 6% p.a. for the first 2 years, 9% p.a. for the next 3 years, and 14% p.a. for the period beyond 5 years. If total interest after 9 years is Rs. 11,400, find the principal.
In how much time will simple interest on Rs. 500 at 5% per annum be equal to simple interest on Rs. 600 at 4.5% per annum in 5 years?
A sum of money at simple interest becomes 7/6 of itself in 3 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?
A sum of Rs. 10,000 is lent in two parts: one at 8% and the other at 10%. If the average annual interest is 9.2%, find the amount lent at 8%.
A person deposited Rs. 400 for 2 years, Rs. 550 for 4 years, and Rs. 1,200 for 6 years at the same simple interest rate. Total interest received was Rs. 1,020. What was the rate of interest?
A sum of money invested at simple interest doubles in 5 years. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.explanation: Time to become n times = [(n - 1) / (2 - 1)] * T1 = [(8 - 1) / 1] * 5 = 7 * 5 = 35 years.

questions.questionText: If the annual rate of simple interest increases from 10% to 12.5%, a man's yearly income increases by Rs. 1,250. Find the principal.
A debt of Rs. 848 is to be paid off in 4 equal annual installments at 4% per annum simple interest. Find each installment.
A sum of money was lent at a certain rate of simple interest for 4 years. If it had been lent at 2% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 560 more. Find the sum.
At what simple interest rate will a sum of Rs. 3,000 amount to Rs. 3,900 in 5 years?
The simple interest on a sum for 5 years is 3/5 of the principal. What is the rate of interest per annum?
A sum of money invested at simple interest amounts to Rs. 2,240 in 2 years and Rs. 2,600 in 5 years. Find the principal and the rate of interest.
questions.explanation: SI for 3 years = 2600 - 2240 = Rs. 360. SI for 1 year = Rs. 120. SI for 2 years = Rs. 240. Principal = 2240 - 240 = Rs. 2000. Rate = (120 / 2000) * 100% = 6%.

questions.questionText: In what time will simple interest on Rs. 400 at 10% per annum be Rs. 200?
A lent Rs. 5,000 to B for 2 years and Rs. 3,000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate. He received Rs. 2,200 in all from both as interest. Find the rate of interest.
A sum of money becomes 5 times itself in 20 years at simple interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
If simple interest on a sum of money for 2 years at 5% p.a. is Rs. 50, what will be the simple interest on the same sum for 3 years at 6% p.a.?
A sum of Rs. 1,875 was lent out partly at 4% and partly at 6% simple interest. Total interest in 2 years was Rs. 180. Find the sum lent at 4%.
What principal will amount to Rs. 560 in 3 years at 4% simple interest per annum?
If simple interest on a sum for 8 years is equal to the principal, find the rate percent per annum.
A person borrows Rs. 8,000 at 5% simple interest and repays Rs. 2,000 at the end of every year. What is the total interest paid over 3 years?
questions.explanation: Year 1 interest: 5% of 8000 = Rs. 400. Year 2 interest on remaining (8000-2000=6000): 5% of 6000 = Rs. 300. Year 3 interest on remaining (6000-2000=4000): 5% of 4000 = Rs. 200. Total interest = 400 + 300 + 200 = Rs. 900.

questions.questionText: A sum of money amounts to Rs. 9,800 in 5 years and Rs. 12,005 in 8 years at the same rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest.
If the simple interest on a certain sum of money is Rs. 256 and the rate of interest is equal to the number of years, find the rate of interest if the principal is Rs. 1,600.
Which of the following Venn diagrams best represents the relationship among: "Musicians", "Violinists", and "Instrumentalists"?
questions.optionB: Two intersecting circles completely outside the third circle
questions.optionC: Violinists and Musicians intersecting, with Instrumentalists disjoint
questions.optionD: Three concentric circles with Violinists innermost, Instrumentalists in middle, and Musicians outermost
questions.explanation: All violinists are instrumentalists (since the violin is an instrument), and all instrumentalists are musicians. Thus, Violinists is a subset of Instrumentalists, which in turn is a subset of Musicians. This is represented by three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a college class of 100 students, 60 play Cricket, 50 play Football, and 20 play both sports. How many students play neither Cricket nor Football?
questions.explanation: Using the formula: n(C union F) = n(C) + n(F) - n(C intersect F) = 60 + 50 - 20 = 90 students play at least one sport. The number of students playing neither sport = Total - n(C union F) = 100 - 90 = 10 students.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram best illustrates the relationship among: "Doctors", "Smokers", and "Females"?
questions.optionA: Two disjoint circles inside a third large circle
questions.optionB: Three mutually intersecting circles overlapping at a common central region
questions.optionD: One circle containing two other intersecting circles
questions.explanation: Some doctors are females, some doctors are smokers, and some female doctors smoke. Thus, each category partially overlaps with the other two, represented by three intersecting circles with a common central region.

questions.questionText: In a survey of 120 people, 70 drink Tea, 60 drink Coffee, and 15 drink neither beverage. How many people drink both Tea and Coffee?
questions.explanation: Total drinking at least one beverage = 120 - 15 = 105. Formula: n(T union C) = n(T) + n(C) - n(T intersect C). 105 = 70 + 60 - Both => 105 = 130 - Both => Both = 130 - 105 = 25 people.

questions.questionText: Which of the following geometric figures best represents the relationship among: "Mammals", "Dogs", and "Cats"?
questions.optionD: A large circle containing two separate, non-overlapping circles inside it
questions.explanation: Both Dogs and Cats are Mammals (subsets of Mammals), but no dog is a cat (Dogs and Cats are completely disjoint). This is represented by a large enclosing circle with two separate non-overlapping circles inside.

questions.questionText: In a group of 80 IT professionals, 45 know Python, 40 know Java, and 15 know both languages. How many professionals know ONLY Python?
questions.explanation: Number of professionals knowing ONLY Python = Total Python - Both = 45 - 15 = 30 professionals.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram correctly represents the relationship among: "States", "Districts", and "Cities"?
questions.optionB: Three concentric circles (Cities inside Districts, Districts inside States)
questions.optionC: Two intersecting circles inside a third circle
questions.explanation: A city is located within a district, and a district is located within a state. Hence, Cities is a subset of Districts, which is a subset of States. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a competitive exam of 200 candidates, 110 passed Quantitative Aptitude, 120 passed Logical Reasoning, and 50 passed both sections. How many candidates failed both sections?
questions.explanation: Passed at least one section: n(Q union L) = n(Q) + n(L) - n(Q intersect L) = 110 + 120 - 50 = 180. Failed both sections = 200 - 180 = 20 candidates.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram best illustrates the relationship among: "Birds", "Bats", and "Owls"?
questions.optionA: A large circle containing two intersecting circles
questions.optionD: A large circle (Birds) containing a smaller circle (Owls), with a completely separate circle outside (Bats)
questions.explanation: Owls are birds (Owls is a subset of Birds). Bats are mammals that fly (not birds), so Bats is completely disjoint from Birds and Owls.

questions.questionText: In a housing society of 150 residents, 90 subscribe to Newspaper A, 70 subscribe to Newspaper B, and 30 subscribe to neither. How many residents subscribe ONLY to Newspaper B?
questions.explanation: Residents subscribing to at least one paper = 150 - 30 = 120. Formula: 120 = 90 + 70 - Both => Both = 160 - 120 = 40. Subscribing ONLY to Newspaper B = Total B - Both = 70 - 40 = 30 residents.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Professors", "Researchers", and "Scientists"?
questions.optionB: Three mutually intersecting circles overlapping in a central region
questions.optionC: One circle containing two disjoint circles
questions.explanation: A person can be both a professor and a researcher, a researcher and a scientist, or all three simultaneously. Thus, three mutually intersecting circles best represents the relationship.

questions.questionText: In a software company, 60 engineers work on Frontend, 55 work on Backend, and 25 work on both. If 10 engineers work on neither, how many total engineers are in the company?
questions.explanation: Total working on at least one = Frontend + Backend - Both = 60 + 55 - 25 = 90 engineers. Total engineers = 90 + 10 (neither) = 100 engineers.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Vegetables", "Potatoes", and "Apples"?
questions.optionC: A large circle containing both Potatoes and Apples intersecting each other
questions.optionD: A large circle (Vegetables) containing Potatoes, with Apples as a separate disjoint circle
questions.explanation: Potato is a vegetable (subset of Vegetables). Apple is a fruit, completely separate from vegetables. Thus, Vegetables contains Potatoes, and Apples is a disjoint circle outside.

questions.questionText: In a batch of 90 students, 40 study French, 35 study Spanish, and 15 study both languages. How many students study Spanish but NOT French?
questions.explanation: Students studying Spanish but NOT French = Total Spanish - Both = 35 - 15 = 20 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Earth", "Planets", and "Moon"?
questions.optionB: A large circle (Planets) containing Earth, with Moon as an independent disjoint circle outside
questions.optionD: A circle containing both Earth and Moon
questions.explanation: Earth is a planet (subset of Planets). The Moon is a natural satellite, not a planet. Thus, Planets contains Earth, and Moon is a disjoint circle.

questions.questionText: In a gym of 75 members, 45 lift weights, 30 do cardio, and 10 do neither. How many members do BOTH weights and cardio?
questions.explanation: Members doing at least one = 75 - 10 = 65. Weights + Cardio - Both = 65 => 45 + 30 - Both = 65 => 75 - Both = 65 => Both = 10 members.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Tables", "Chairs", and "Furniture"?
questions.optionD: A large circle (Furniture) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Tables and Chairs)
questions.explanation: Both Tables and Chairs belong to the broader category of Furniture, but a table is not a chair. Thus, a large circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In a test of 60 students, 35 passed Physics and 30 passed Chemistry. If every student passed at least one of the two subjects, how many students passed BOTH Physics and Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Since every student passed at least one: n(P union C) = 60. Formula: 60 = 35 + 30 - Both => 60 = 65 - Both => Both = 65 - 60 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Elephants", "Carnivores", and "Tigers"?
questions.optionB: A circle (Carnivores) containing Tigers, with Elephants completely outside as a disjoint circle
questions.optionD: Carnivores containing both Elephants and Tigers
questions.explanation: Tigers are obligate carnivores (subset of Carnivores). Elephants are herbivores (completely disjoint from Carnivores and Tigers). Hence, Carnivores contains Tigers, with Elephants separate.

questions.questionText: In an office of 110 employees, 70 drink Green Tea, 50 drink Black Tea, and 20 drink both. How many drink NEITHER Green Tea nor Black Tea?
questions.explanation: Union = 70 + 50 - 20 = 100 employees drink at least one type of tea. Neither = Total - Union = 110 - 100 = 10 employees.

questions.questionText: In a college of 200 students: 100 play Cricket, 80 play Football, and 70 play Hockey. 40 play Cricket and Football, 30 play Football and Hockey, 35 play Cricket and Hockey, and 15 play all three sports. How many students play at least one of these three sports?
questions.explanation: Formula: n(A union B union C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(AB) - n(BC) - n(AC) + n(ABC) = 100 + 80 + 70 - 40 - 30 - 35 + 15 = 250 - 105 + 15 = 160 students.

questions.questionText: In a cohort of 100 engineering students: 50 know C++, 40 know Java, and 30 know Python. 20 know C++ and Java, 15 know Java and Python, 10 know C++ and Python, and 5 know all three languages. How many students know NONE of these three programming languages?
questions.explanation: At least one language: n(C union J union P) = 50 + 40 + 30 - 20 - 15 - 10 + 5 = 120 - 45 + 5 = 80 students. Students knowing none = Total - 80 = 100 - 80 = 20 students.

questions.questionText: In a market survey of 150 consumers: 80 purchase Brand A, 65 purchase Brand B, and 55 purchase Brand C. 30 purchase Brands A and B, 25 purchase Brands B and C, 20 purchase Brands A and C, and 10 purchase all three brands. How many consumers purchase ONLY Brand A?
questions.explanation: Only Brand A = Total A - (AB + AC - ABC) = 80 - (30 + 20 - 10) = 80 - 40 = 40 consumers.

questions.questionText: In a class of 80 students, 30 like Math, 35 like Science, and 40 like English. 12 like Math and Science, 15 like Science and English, 10 like Math and English, and 5 like all three subjects. How many students like EXACTLY TWO of these three subjects?
questions.explanation: In a 3-set Venn diagram, the region representing exactly two subjects is: (n(MS) - n(MSE)) + (n(SE) - n(MSE)) + (n(ME) - n(MSE)) = (12 - 5) + (15 - 5) + (10 - 5) = 7 + 10 + 5 = 22 students.

questions.questionText: In a survey of 120 music listeners: 65 listen to Rock, 55 listen to Pop, and 45 listen to Classical. 25 listen to Rock and Pop, 20 listen to Pop and Classical, 15 listen to Rock and Classical, and 10 listen to all three genres. How many listen to EXACTLY ONE genre?
questions.explanation: Only Rock = 65 - (25 + 15 - 10) = 65 - 30 = 35. Only Pop = 55 - (25 + 20 - 10) = 55 - 35 = 20. Only Classical = 45 - (20 + 15 - 10) = 45 - 25 = 20. Exactly one genre = Only Rock + Only Pop + Only Classical = 35 + 20 + 20 = 75 listeners.

questions.questionText: In a university department of 60 professors, 30 speak French, 25 speak German, and 20 speak Russian. 10 speak French and German, 8 speak German and Russian, 7 speak French and Russian, and 3 speak all three languages. How many professors speak French and German but NOT Russian?
questions.explanation: French and German but NOT Russian corresponds directly to the region (French intersect German) minus all three: n(F intersect G) - n(F intersect G intersect R) = 10 - 3 = 7 professors.

questions.questionText: In a residential society of 200 residents: 110 read English newspaper, 90 read Hindi newspaper, and 60 read Regional newspaper. 40 read English and Hindi, 30 read Hindi and Regional, 25 read English and Regional, and 15 read all three. How many residents read ONLY the Hindi newspaper?
questions.explanation: Only Hindi = Total Hindi - (Hindi & English + Hindi & Regional - All three) = 90 - (40 + 30 - 15) = 90 - 55 = 35 residents.

questions.questionText: A sports academy has 100 athletes. 48 train in Swimming, 45 in Running, and 40 in Cycling. 18 do Swimming and Running, 15 do Running and Cycling, 12 do Swimming and Cycling, and 5 do all three. How many athletes train in NEITHER of these three sports?

In a group of 50 students, 28 like Chocolate ice cream, 24 like Vanilla, and 20 like Strawberry. 10 like Chocolate and Vanilla, 8 like Vanilla and Strawberry, 7 like Chocolate and Strawberry, and 4 like all three. How many students like Chocolate and Strawberry but NOT Vanilla?
questions.explanation: The region liking Chocolate and Strawberry without Vanilla is n(C intersect S) - n(C intersect V intersect S) = 7 - 4 = 3 students.

questions.questionText: In a library, 70 visitors read Fiction, 50 read Non-Fiction, and 40 read Science. 20 read Fiction and Non-Fiction, 15 read Non-Fiction and Science, 12 read Fiction and Science, and 8 read all three. How many visitors read Science but NEITHER Fiction NOR Non-Fiction?
questions.explanation: Only Science = Total Science - (Fiction & Science + Non-Fiction & Science - All three) = 40 - (12 + 15 - 8) = 40 - 19 = 21 visitors.

questions.questionText: In an exam taken by 150 students, 90 passed Mathematics, 80 passed Physics, and 75 passed Chemistry. 45 passed Math and Physics, 40 passed Physics and Chemistry, 35 passed Math and Chemistry, and 20 passed all three. How many students failed in ALL three subjects?
questions.explanation: Passed at least one = 90 + 80 + 75 - 45 - 40 - 35 + 20 = 245 - 120 + 20 = 145 students. Failed all three = 150 - 145 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Professions", "Architects", and "Civil Engineers"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Professions) containing two intersecting circles (Architects and Civil Engineers)
questions.optionD: Professions containing two separate disjoint circles
questions.explanation: Both Architects and Civil Engineers are Professions (subsets of Professions). Some people hold qualifications in both architecture and civil engineering (dual-degree professionals). Thus, a large circle encloses two intersecting circles.

questions.questionText: In a tech incubator of 90 founders, 50 have technical backgrounds, 45 have business backgrounds, and 35 have design backgrounds. 20 have both tech and business, 15 have business and design, 12 have tech and design, and 5 have all three. How many founders have ONLY a design background?
questions.explanation: Only design = Total Design - (Tech & Design + Business & Design - All three) = 35 - (12 + 15 - 5) = 35 - 22 = 13 founders.

questions.questionText: In a sample of 250 voters: 130 favor Policy A, 110 favor Policy B, and 95 favor Policy C. 55 favor A and B, 45 favor B and C, 40 favor A and C, and 20 favor all three. How many voters favor at least one of the three policies?
questions.explanation: At least one policy: n(A union B union C) = 130 + 110 + 95 - 55 - 45 - 40 + 20 = 335 - 140 + 20 = 215 voters.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best illustrates: "Reptiles", "Snakes", and "Lizards"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Reptiles) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Snakes and Lizards)
questions.explanation: Snakes and Lizards are both Reptiles, but no snake is a lizard (distinct suborders Serpentes and Lacertilia). Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In a club of 70 members, 35 play Chess, 30 play Scrabble, and 25 play Bridge. 12 play Chess and Scrabble, 10 play Scrabble and Bridge, 8 play Chess and Bridge, and 4 play all three. How many members play EXACTLY TWO games?
questions.explanation: Exactly two games = (Chess&Scrabble - All) + (Scrabble&Bridge - All) + (Chess&Bridge - All) = (12 - 4) + (10 - 4) + (8 - 4) = 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 members.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Quadrilaterals", "Rectangles", and "Squares"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles with Squares inside Rectangles, and Rectangles inside Quadrilaterals
questions.optionC: A circle containing two separate circles
questions.explanation: All squares are rectangles, and all rectangles are quadrilaterals. This forms a strict chain of subset inclusion, represented by three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a hospital staff of 80 nurses, 40 have ICU certification, 35 have ER certification, and 30 have Pediatric certification. 15 have ICU & ER, 12 have ER & Pediatric, 10 have ICU & Pediatric, and 5 have all three certifications. How many nurses have ONLY ICU certification?
questions.explanation: Only ICU = Total ICU - (ICU & ER + ICU & Pediatric - All three) = 40 - (15 + 10 - 5) = 40 - 20 = 20 nurses.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Liquids", "Water", and "Oil"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Liquids) enclosing two disjoint circles (Water and Oil)
questions.explanation: Both Water and Oil are liquids, but water is not oil (immiscible, chemically distinct). A large circle contains two non-overlapping circles.

questions.questionText: In a test batch of 100 components, 45 passed Stress Test, 40 passed Temperature Test, and 35 passed Vibration Test. 15 passed Stress & Temp, 12 passed Temp & Vibration, 10 passed Stress & Vibration, and 4 passed all three. How many components passed Temperature and Vibration tests but FAILED the Stress test?
questions.explanation: Passed Temperature and Vibration but not Stress = (Temp intersect Vibration) - All three = 12 - 4 = 8 components.

questions.questionText: In an international summit of 120 delegates: 70 speak English, 60 speak French, and 50 speak Spanish. 30 speak English and French, 25 speak French and Spanish, 20 speak English and Spanish, and 10 speak all three languages. How many delegates speak EXACTLY ONE of these three languages?
questions.explanation: Only English = 70 - (30 + 20 - 10) = 70 - 40 = 30. Only French = 60 - (30 + 25 - 10) = 60 - 45 = 15. Only Spanish = 50 - (25 + 20 - 10) = 50 - 35 = 15. Exactly one language = 30 + 15 + 15 = 60 delegates. Wait: let us check option: "60". Correct: 60.

questions.questionText: In a corporate survey, out of 300 employees: 180 use Slack, 140 use Teams, and 100 use Zoom. 80 use Slack and Teams, 50 use Teams and Zoom, 40 use Slack and Zoom, and 20 use all three tools. How many employees use AT LEAST TWO of these communication tools?
questions.explanation: At least two tools = (Slack&Teams only) + (Teams&Zoom only) + (Slack&Zoom only) + All three = (80 - 20) + (50 - 20) + (40 - 20) + 20 = 60 + 30 + 20 + 20 = 130 employees.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Fathers", "Males", and "Engineers"?
questions.optionB: A circle of Males completely containing Fathers, with Engineers intersecting both Males and Fathers
questions.optionD: Males and Fathers intersecting outside Engineers
questions.explanation: All fathers are biologically males (Fathers is a strict subset of Males). Some engineers are fathers, some engineers are males who are not fathers, and some engineers are females (neither fathers nor males). Thus, Engineers intersects both Males and the inner Fathers circle.

questions.questionText: In a school of 200 students: 120 participate in Music, 100 in Dance, and 80 in Drama. 50 in Music & Dance, 40 in Dance & Drama, 35 in Music & Drama, and 20 in all three. How many students participate in NONE of these three activities?

In a company of 80 employees: 42 drink Tea, 38 drink Coffee, and 30 drink Juice. 16 drink Tea and Coffee, 14 drink Coffee and Juice, 12 drink Tea and Juice, and 6 drink all three. How many drink Tea and Juice but NOT Coffee?
questions.explanation: Tea and Juice but NOT Coffee = n(Tea intersect Juice) - n(Tea intersect Coffee intersect Juice) = 12 - 6 = 6 employees.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Polygons", "Triangles", and "Scalene Triangles"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles (Scalene Triangles inside Triangles, Triangles inside Polygons)
questions.explanation: Every scalene triangle is a triangle, and every triangle is a polygon. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In an algorithm test taken by 100 students: 60 solved Problem 1, 50 solved Problem 2, and 45 solved Problem 3. 25 solved Problems 1 & 2, 20 solved Problems 2 & 3, 15 solved Problems 1 & 3, and 5 solved all three problems. How many students solved ONLY Problem 1?
questions.explanation: Only Problem 1 = Total Problem 1 - (1&2 + 1&3 - All three) = 60 - (25 + 15 - 5) = 60 - 35 = 25 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Lawyers", "Females", and "Mothers"?
questions.optionC: A circle of Females completely containing Mothers, with Lawyers intersecting both Females and Mothers
questions.explanation: All mothers are females (Mothers is a subset of Females). Some lawyers are mothers, some lawyers are females who are not mothers, and some lawyers are males (outside Females). Thus, Lawyers intersects both Females and the subset Mothers.

questions.questionText: In a consumer study of 150 gadget owners: 85 own a Tablet, 75 own a Laptop, and 60 own a Smartwatch. 35 own Tablet & Laptop, 25 own Laptop & Smartwatch, 20 own Tablet & Smartwatch, and 10 own all three gadgets. How many own a Laptop and Smartwatch but NOT a Tablet?
questions.explanation: Laptop and Smartwatch without Tablet = (Laptop intersect Smartwatch) - All three = 25 - 10 = 15 owners.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Currency", "Yen", and "Euro"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Currency) containing two separate non-overlapping circles (Yen and Euro)
questions.explanation: Both Yen and Euro are currencies (subsets of Currency), but Yen is not Euro (distinct currencies). Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an audit of 160 tax filings: 90 claimed Deduction A, 80 claimed Deduction B, and 70 claimed Deduction C. 40 claimed A & B, 30 claimed B & C, 25 claimed A & C, and 15 claimed all three. How many tax filings claimed EXACTLY ONE deduction?
Which diagram represents: "Atmospheric Gases", "Oxygen", and "Nitrogen"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Atmospheric Gases) containing two separate non-overlapping circles (Oxygen and Nitrogen)
questions.explanation: Both Oxygen and Nitrogen are atmospheric gases, but Oxygen is chemically distinct from Nitrogen. Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an e-commerce platform survey of 120 shoppers: 65 bought Clothing, 50 bought Footwear, and 45 bought Accessories. 25 bought Clothing & Footwear, 20 bought Footwear & Accessories, 15 bought Clothing & Accessories, and 8 bought all three categories. How many shoppers bought AT LEAST ONE of these three categories?
Which diagram best represents: "Animals", "Herbivores", and "Deer"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles (Deer inside Herbivores, Herbivores inside Animals)
questions.explanation: All deer are herbivores, and all herbivores are animals. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a tournament of 100 chess players: 55 know the Sicilian Defense, 45 know the French Defense, and 35 know the Caro-Kann Defense. 20 know Sicilian & French, 15 know French & Caro-Kann, 10 know Sicilian & Caro-Kann, and 5 know all three openings. How many players know EXACTLY TWO openings?
questions.explanation: Exactly two openings = (20 - 5) + (15 - 5) + (10 - 5) = 15 + 10 + 5 = 30 players.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Planets", "Mars", and "Jupiter"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Planets) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Mars and Jupiter)
questions.explanation: Both Mars and Jupiter are planets, but Mars is distinct from Jupiter. A large enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an academic batch of 80 students: 40 like Algebra, 35 like Geometry, and 30 like Calculus. 15 like Algebra & Geometry, 12 like Geometry & Calculus, 10 like Algebra & Calculus, and 5 like all three. How many students like Algebra and Calculus but NOT Geometry?
questions.explanation: Algebra and Calculus without Geometry = (Algebra intersect Calculus) - All three = 10 - 5 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Writers", "Poets", and "Novelist"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Writers) containing two intersecting circles (Poets and Novelists)
questions.explanation: Poets and Novelists are both Writers (subsets of Writers). Some writers write both poetry and novels (intersection). Thus, Writers encloses two intersecting circles.

questions.questionText: In a test of 90 students: 50 passed Section A, 45 passed Section B, and 40 passed Section C. 20 passed A & B, 15 passed B & C, 12 passed A & C, and 5 passed all three. How many students passed ONLY Section B?
questions.explanation: Only Section B = Total B - (AB + BC - ABC) = 45 - (20 + 15 - 5) = 45 - 30 = 15 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Automobiles", "Sedans", and "SUVs"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Automobiles) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Sedans and SUVs)
questions.explanation: Both Sedans and SUVs are Automobiles, but a sedan is not an SUV (distinct vehicle body types). An enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must tea at Rs. 62 per kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 72 per kg so that the mixture must be worth Rs. 64.50 per kg?
A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. This process is repeated two more times. How much milk is now left in the vessel?
questions.explanation: Formula: Remaining pure liquid = Initial * (1 - x / V)^n. Remaining milk = 80 * (1 - 8/80)^3 = 80 * (0.9)^3 = 80 * 0.729 = 58.32 litres.

questions.questionText: A merchant has 1000 kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. What is the quantity sold at 18% profit?
How many kg of rice at Rs. 54 per kg should be mixed with 30 kg of rice at Rs. 40 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 57.60 per kg there is a gain of 20%?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 57.60 / 1.20 = Rs. 48 per kg. Alligation between Rs. 54 and Rs. 40 to get Rs. 48: Ratio = (48 - 40) : (54 - 48) = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. For 3 parts = 30 kg, 4 parts = 40 kg.

questions.questionText: Two vessels A and B contain milk and water in the ratios 7 : 5 and 17 : 7 respectively. In what ratio should the mixtures from A and B be mixed to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.explanation: Milk fraction in A = 7/12. Milk fraction in B = 17/24. Target milk fraction = 3/5. By Alligation: (17/24 - 3/5) : (3/5 - 7/12) = (85 - 72)/120 : (36 - 35)/60 = (13/120) : (2/120) = 13 : 2.

questions.questionText: A jar contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 litres of the mixture is taken out and 10 litres of liquid B is poured in, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. How many litres of liquid A was contained in the jar initially?
questions.explanation: Let initial quantities be 4x and x. When 10 L is removed: A removed = 8 L, B removed = 2 L. (4x - 8) / (x - 2 + 10) = 2/3 => (4x - 8)/(x + 8) = 2/3 => 3(4x - 8) = 2(x + 8) => 12x - 24 = 2x + 16 => 10x = 40 => x = 4. Initial liquid A = 4 * 4 = 16 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio should water be mixed with milk costing Rs. 12 per litre so as to make a profit of 20% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.explanation: When sold at CP, Profit% = (Water / Milk) * 100% = 20% => Water / Milk = 20 / 100 = 1 / 5.

questions.questionText: A can contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 7 : 5. When 9 litres of mixture are drawn off and the can is filled with B, the ratio of A and B becomes 7 : 9. How many litres of liquid A was contained by the can initially?
The cost of Type 1 rice is Rs. 15 per kg and Type 2 rice is Rs. 20 per kg. If both are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3, then the price per kg of the mixed variety of rice is:
In a 729 litre mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk to water is 7 : 2. How much water should be added to get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 9. 1 part = 729 / 9 = 81 litres. Initial milk = 7 * 81 = 567 L, Water = 2 * 81 = 162 L. In new ratio 7 : 3, milk remains 567 L (7 parts => 1 part = 81 L). Required water = 3 * 81 = 243 L. Water to add = 243 - 162 = 81 litres.
questions.concept: Adding Water to Fixed Milk Baseline

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of pulses costing Rs. 15 and Rs. 20 per kg respectively so as to get a mixture worth Rs. 16.50 per kg?
A 20-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much milk should be added to make the ratio 4 : 1?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 15 L, Water = 5 L. To make ratio 4 : 1 with 5 L water, total milk required = 4 * 5 = 20 L. Milk to add = 20 - 15 = 5 litres.
questions.concept: Milk Addition to Fixed Water Baseline

questions.questionText: A container contains 40 litres of milk. From this container, 4 litres of milk was taken out and replaced by water. This process was repeated further two times. How much milk is now contained by the container?
Two alloys A and B contain zinc and tin in the ratios 5 : 2 and 3 : 4 respectively. If 7 kg of alloy A and 21 kg of alloy B are mixed together, find the ratio of zinc to tin in the new alloy.
questions.explanation: Alloy A (7 kg): Zinc = 5 kg, Tin = 2 kg. Alloy B (21 kg, ratio 3:4, total 7 parts => 1 part = 3 kg): Zinc = 3 * 3 = 9 kg, Tin = 4 * 3 = 12 kg. Total Zinc = 5 + 9 = 14 kg. Total Tin = 2 + 12 = 14 kg. Ratio = 14 : 14 = 1 : 1.

questions.questionText: How many kg of sugar costing Rs. 9 per kg must be mixed with 27 kg of sugar costing Rs. 7 per kg so that there may be a gain of 10% by selling the mixture at Rs. 9.24 per kg?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 9.24 / 1.10 = Rs. 8.40 per kg. Alligation between Rs. 9 and Rs. 7 to get Rs. 8.40: Ratio = (8.40 - 7) : (9 - 8.40) = 1.40 : 0.60 = 7 : 3. 3 parts = 27 kg => 1 part = 9 kg. 7 parts = 7 * 9 = 63 kg.

questions.questionText: A vessel of 60 litres is full of milk. 12 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. Again 12 litres of mixture is taken out and replaced by water. Find the ratio of milk and water in the final mixture.
In what ratio must a 30% alcohol solution be mixed with a 50% alcohol solution to get a 35% alcohol solution?
A mixture of 40 litres of milk and water contains 10% water. How much water should be added to this so that water may be 20% in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk in initial mixture = 90% of 40 = 36 litres. In new mixture, milk is 80%. Let total new mixture be T. 80% of T = 36 => T = 36 / 0.80 = 45 litres. Water to add = 45 - 40 = 5 litres.

questions.questionText: Two containers have milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1 and 5 : 3. If equal quantities are taken from both and mixed, find the ratio of milk to water in the resulting mixture.
questions.explanation: Container 1 (total 4 parts, scale by 2): Milk = 6/8, Water = 2/8. Container 2 (total 8 parts): Milk = 5/8, Water = 3/8. Total Milk = 6 + 5 = 11. Total Water = 2 + 3 = 5. Resulting ratio = 11 : 5.

questions.questionText: A butler steals wine from a butt of sherry containing 40% spirit and replaces what he stole with wine containing 16% spirit. The butt is then of 24% strength. How much of the butt did he steal?
questions.explanation: By Alligation: Original (40%) and Stolen Replacement (16%) mix to (24%). Ratio of original remaining to replaced = (24 - 16) : (40 - 24) = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2. Total butt = 1 + 2 = 3 parts. Stolen & replaced portion = 2 / 3.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must water be mixed with milk to gain 16 2/3% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.explanation: Gain% = 16 2/3 % = 50/3 % = 1/6. Ratio of water to milk = 1 : 6.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 50 litres of milk. 10 litres is taken out and replaced by water. 10 litres is again taken out and replaced by water. How much milk is left in the vessel?
Gold is 19 times as heavy as water and copper is 9 times as heavy as water. In what ratio should these be mixed to get an alloy 15 times as heavy as water?
A mixture of 150 litres of wine and water contains 20% water. How much more water should be added so that water becomes 25% of the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Wine = 80% of 150 = 120 L. In new mixture, wine is 75%. Total new mixture = 120 / 0.75 = 160 L. Water added = 160 - 150 = 10 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must tea at Rs. 240/kg be mixed with tea at Rs. 280/kg so that the mixture is worth Rs. 260/kg?

Three glasses of equal volume contain mixture of milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1, 3 : 1, and 3 : 2. If all three are poured into a single vessel, find the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture.
questions.explanation: Volumes: 3, 4, 5. LCM = 60. Glass 1 (scale 20): Milk = 40, Water = 20. Glass 2 (scale 15): Milk = 45, Water = 15. Glass 3 (scale 12): Milk = 36, Water = 24. Total Milk = 40 + 45 + 36 = 121. Total Water = 20 + 15 + 24 = 59. Ratio = 121 : 59.

questions.questionText: A trader has 50 kg of pulses, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. What is the quantity sold at 18% profit?
A vessel contains 60 litres of pure acid. 10 litres is taken out and replaced by water. Then 10 litres of the mixture is taken out and replaced by water. What is the amount of pure acid left?
A 45-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 36 L, Water = 9 L. For ratio 3 : 2 with 36 L milk: 3 parts = 36 => 1 part = 12 L. Water needed = 2 * 12 = 24 L. Water to add = 24 - 9 = 15 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio should two qualities of coffee powder costing Rs. 180 and Rs. 260 per kg be mixed to obtain a blend worth Rs. 210 per kg?
A milkman has 20 litres of milk. He mixes 5 litres of water. What is the percentage of milk in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Total volume = 25 L. Milk = 20 L. Percentage = (20 / 25) * 100% = 80%.

questions.questionText: Two vessels contain milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2 and 7 : 3. In what ratio should the contents of the two vessels be mixed to get a mixture containing milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1?
From a cask of 63 litres of wine, 9 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. If this is done twice in total, how much wine remains in the cask?
questions.explanation: After each replacement, the fraction of wine retained is 1 - 9/63 = 6/7. After two rounds, the wine remaining is 63*(6/7)^2 = 324/7 litres, or about 46.29 litres.

questions.questionText: A 35-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. If 7 litres of water is added, what will be the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.explanation: Initial: Milk = 28 L, Water = 7 L. Adding 7 L water: New Water = 14 L. New ratio = 28 : 14 = 2 : 1.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must grocer mix two varieties of tea worth Rs. 60/kg and Rs. 65/kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 68.20/kg he gains 10%?
A container has 50 litres of juice. 5 litres is drawn out and replaced with water. This process is repeated 3 times. What is the percentage of juice left?

Two vessels A and B contain spirits and water in the ratio 5 : 2 and 7 : 6 respectively. Find the ratio in which these mixtures be mixed to obtain a new mixture in vessel C containing spirit and water in the ratio 8 : 5?
How much water should be added to 300 ml of 20% acid solution to make it a 15% acid solution?
questions.explanation: Acid = 20% of 300 = 60 ml. In 15% solution, total volume = 60 / 0.15 = 400 ml. Water to add = 400 - 300 = 100 ml.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains a mixture of 1 part water and 3 parts syrup. How much of the mixture must be drawn off and replaced with water so that the mixture may be half water and half syrup?
questions.explanation: Syrup initially = 3/4. Target syrup = 1/2. Let fraction removed and replaced with water (0% syrup) be x. (3/4)(1 - x) = 1/2 => 1 - x = (1/2)*(4/3) = 2/3 => x = 1/3.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must an alloy containing 80% copper be mixed with an alloy containing 90% copper to obtain an alloy containing 84% copper?
In what ratio must water be mixed with milk to gain 20% by selling the mixture at cost price?
questions.concept: Direct Water Ratio on CP Sale

questions.questionText: A merchant has 120 kg of wheat, part of which he sells at 10% gain and the rest at 25% gain. Overall he gains 15%. How much wheat was sold at 25% gain?
A jar contains 60 litres of milk. 12 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. If this process is repeated twice more (total 3 times), find the quantity of milk remaining.

Two vessels A and B contain mixtures of milk and water in the ratio 4 : 5 and 5 : 1 respectively. In what ratio should quantities be taken from A and B to form a mixture in which milk and water are in the ratio 5 : 4?
questions.explanation: Milk in A = 4/9 = 8/18. Milk in B = 5/6 = 15/18. Target milk in mixture = 5/9 = 10/18. By Alligation: (15/18 - 10/18) : (10/18 - 8/18) = 5 : 2.

questions.questionText: How many kg of salt at 42 paise per kg must a man mix with 25 kg of salt at 24 paise per kg so that he may gain 25% by selling the mixture at 40 paise per kg?
questions.explanation: Mean CP = 40 / 1.25 = 32 paise/kg. By Alligation: (32 - 24) : (42 - 32) = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5. 5 parts = 25 kg => 1 part = 5 kg. 4 parts = 4 * 5 = 20 kg.

questions.questionText: A 40-litre mixture of milk and water contains 10% water. How many litres of water must be added to make water 20% in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk = 90% of 40 = 36 L. In new mixture: 80% = 36 L => Total = 45 L. Water to add = 45 - 40 = 5 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a merchant mix two varieties of oil costing Rs. 70/litre and Rs. 90/litre to obtain a mixture worth Rs. 78/litre?

A cask contains 100 litres of wine. 10 litres of wine is drawn and replaced by water. 10 litres of mixture is drawn again and replaced by water. Find the ratio of wine to water in the resulting mixture.
A mixture of 125 gallons of wine and water contains 20% wine. How much wine must be added to make it 25% of the total mixture?
questions.explanation: Water = 80% of 125 = 100 gallons. In new mixture, water is 75%. New total = 100 / 0.75 = 133.33 gallons. Wine to add = 133.33 - 125 = 8.33 gallons (8 1/3 gal).

questions.questionText: Two vessels A and B contain mixtures of spirit and water in the ratio 5 : 3 and 2 : 3 respectively. Find the ratio in which these are to be mixed to get a mixture containing half spirit and half water.
A grocer mixes 26 kg of tea at Rs. 20/kg with 30 kg of tea at Rs. 36/kg and sells the mixture at Rs. 30/kg. What is his profit percentage?
A bottle contains 30 litres of milk. 3 litres is taken out and replaced by water. The process is repeated 3 times. What is the quantity of milk in the final mixture?
In what ratio must an 80% acid solution be mixed with a 50% acid solution to produce a 60% acid solution?
A merchant blends two varieties of tea, one costing Rs. 180/kg and another Rs. 200/kg in the ratio 5 : 3. If he sells the blend at Rs. 210/kg, what is his profit percentage?
A mixture contains alcohol and water in the ratio 4 : 3. If 5 litres of water is added to the mixture, the ratio becomes 4 : 5. Find the quantity of alcohol in the given mixture.
From a container of 50 litres of milk, 5 litres is replaced with water. This process is repeated 2 times in total. What is the ratio of milk to water now?
How many litres of water must be added to 16 litres of a 25% salt solution to make it a 20% solution?
questions.explanation: Salt = 25% of 16 = 4 litres. In 20% solution, total volume = 4 / 0.20 = 20 litres. Water to add = 20 - 16 = 4 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must milk and water be mixed so that on selling at cost price, there is a profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: Milk : Water = 100 : 25 = 4 : 1.

questions.questionText: Two alloys of gold and copper contain gold in the ratio 7 : 2 and 7 : 11. If equal weights are melted to form a third alloy C, find the ratio of gold to copper in C.
questions.explanation: Alloy 1 (ratio 7:2, scale by 2): Gold = 14/18, Copper = 4/18. Alloy 2 (ratio 7:11): Gold = 7/18, Copper = 11/18. Total Gold = 14 + 7 = 21. Total Copper = 4 + 11 = 15. Ratio = 21 : 15 = 7 : 5.

questions.questionText: A jar full of whisky contains 40% alcohol. A part of this whisky is replaced by another containing 19% alcohol and now the percentage of alcohol was found to be 26%. What fraction of the whisky was replaced?
In a company of 500 employees, the distribution by department is: IT 30%, Sales 25%, HR 15%, Marketing 20%, and Finance 10%. How many more employees are in IT compared to HR?
questions.explanation: Difference = 30% - 15% = 15% of 500 = 0.15 * 500 = 75 employees.

questions.questionText: A pie chart shows the monthly expenditure of a household. If the angle representing Food is 108Â° and total monthly expenditure is Rs. 36,000, find the amount spent on Food.
The sales of a company over 5 years (in Lakhs Rs.) are: 2020: 45, 2021: 54, 2022: 60, 2023: 75, 2024: 90. What is the percentage growth in sales from 2020 to 2024?
A table shows student scores: Section A (mean 65, n=40), Section B (mean 75, n=60). What is the combined average score of both sections together?
In a line graph showing quarterly profits (Q1: 12L, Q2: 18L, Q3: 15L, Q4: 25L), what is the ratio of average profit of first two quarters to the last two quarters?
A pie chart shows energy consumption: Coal 40%, Petroleum 25%, Natural Gas 20%, Nuclear 10%, Hydro 5%. What central angle corresponds to Natural Gas?
In a survey of 1200 respondents, 45% preferred Product A, 35% preferred Product B, and the rest preferred Product C. How many respondents preferred Product C?
questions.explanation: Percentage for Product C = 100% - (45% + 35%) = 20%. Respondents = 20% of 1200 = 240.

questions.questionText: Production of cars by 3 plants P, Q, R in a year are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. If Plant Q produced 16,000 cars, find the total car production across all three plants.
questions.explanation: 4 parts = 16000 => 1 part = 4000. Total parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts. Total production = 12 * 4000 = 48,000 cars.

questions.questionText: Export data of wheat (in tonnes) for 4 quarters: Q1: 400, Q2: 480, Q3: 520, Q4: 600. What is the quarterly average export of wheat?
In a double bar chart, Company X produced 50,000 units and sold 42,000 units. Company Y produced 60,000 units and sold 48,000 units. Which company had a higher sales-to-production percentage?
questions.explanation: Company X: (42000 / 50000) * 100% = 84%. Company Y: (48000 / 60000) * 100% = 80%. Company X is higher with 84%.

questions.questionText: A pie chart shows expenditure on a book publication: Paper Cost 25%, Printing 20%, Binding 20%, Royalty 15%, Promotion 10%, Transport 10%. If Royalty paid is Rs. 30,000, what is the Printing cost?
questions.explanation: Royalty is 15% = Rs. 30,000 => 1% = Rs. 2,000. Printing cost is 20% = 20 * 2000 = Rs. 40,000.

questions.questionText: In a radar chart showing skill ratings (out of 10) for a candidate: Coding: 9, Logic: 8, Communication: 7, Domain: 8, Aptitude: 8. What is the overall percentage score?
questions.explanation: Total score = 9 + 8 + 7 + 8 + 8 = 40 out of 50. Percentage = (40 / 50) * 100% = 80%.

questions.questionText: A table records annual revenue and expenditure of a firm: Revenue = Rs. 85 Lakhs, Expenditure = Rs. 68 Lakhs. What is the profit margin percentage (Profit / Revenue)?
The pass percentage in three colleges A, B, C are 80%, 75%, and 90% with student strengths 200, 400, and 300 respectively. What is the overall pass percentage across all 3 colleges?
A line graph tracking stock index over 4 weeks: W1: 15000, W2: 15300, W3: 15150, W4: 15604.5. What was the net percentage change from W1 to W4?
In a college library, books by subject are: Science 35%, Arts 25%, Commerce 20%, Literature 15%, Others 5%. If total books are 8,000, how many books are in Science and Arts combined?
questions.explanation: Science + Arts = 35% + 25% = 60%. Combined books = 60% of 8000 = 4,800.

questions.questionText: A stacked bar chart shows expenditure breakdown for Year 1 (Total: 40L, R&D: 8L) and Year 2 (Total: 60L, R&D: 15L). What is the percentage increase in R&D expenditure?
A histogram shows distribution of employee salaries: 10k-20k (15), 20k-30k (25), 30k-40k (35), 40k-50k (20), 50k-60k (5). What percentage of employees earn at least 30k?
questions.explanation: Total employees = 15 + 25 + 35 + 20 + 5 = 100. Employees earning at least 30k = 35 + 20 + 5 = 60. Percentage = 60%.

questions.questionText: A table records production defective rates: Batch 1 (500 units, 2% defective), Batch 2 (300 units, 4% defective), Batch 3 (200 units, 5% defective). What is the overall defect rate?
questions.explanation: Defectives: Batch 1 = 10, Batch 2 = 12, Batch 3 = 10. Total defectives = 32. Total units = 1000. Defect rate = (32 / 1000) * 100% = 3.2%.

questions.questionText: If the central angle in a pie chart representing "Savings" is 54Â°, what percentage of income is saved?

In a bar graph showing rainfall (in mm) for 5 months: June: 120, July: 180, August: 200, Sept: 140, Oct: 60. Which month recorded the highest rainfall and what was its percentage contribution to total monsoon rain?
questions.explanation: Total rainfall = 120 + 180 + 200 + 140 + 60 = 700 mm. Highest is August with 200 mm. Percentage = (200 / 700) * 100% = 28.57%.

questions.questionText: A table shows employee distribution: Males = 60% of total 450 employees. If 40% of males and 30% of females are postgraduates, how many postgraduates are there in total?
questions.explanation: Males = 0.60 * 450 = 270. Females = 180. Postgraduate males = 0.40 * 270 = 108. Postgraduate females = 0.30 * 180 = 54. Total postgraduates = 108 + 54 = 162.

questions.questionText: A line graph tracking monthly website visits: Jan: 50k, Feb: 65k, Mar: 52k, Apr: 78k. What is the percentage increase in visits from Mar to Apr?
A pie chart shows vehicle market share: Sedans 35%, SUVs 40%, Hatchbacks 15%, Trucks 10%. If total vehicles sold is 1,20,000, find the difference in sales between SUVs and Hatchbacks.
questions.explanation: Difference = 40% - 15% = 25% of 1,20,000 = 30,000 vehicles.

questions.questionText: In a double bar chart showing import and export for 3 years: Year 1 (Exp: 40, Imp: 50), Year 2 (Exp: 60, Imp: 45), Year 3 (Exp: 75, Imp: 60). In which years was there a trade surplus (Exports > Imports)?
questions.explanation: Trade surplus: Year 2 (60 > 45) and Year 3 (75 > 60).

questions.questionText: A table records marks in 5 subjects out of 100: Math: 92, Physics: 88, Chemistry: 85, English: 75, CS: 95. What is the aggregate percentage score?
In a pie chart, angles for raw materials are: Steel 120Â°, Cement 90Â°, Timber 60Â°, Labour 50Â°, Others 40Â°. If Steel cost is Rs. 2,40,000, find total project cost.
A table lists store performance: Store A (Sales: Rs. 15L, Profit: 15%), Store B (Sales: Rs. 20L, Profit: 10%), Store C (Sales: Rs. 25L, Profit: 12%). Which store generated highest absolute profit?
questions.explanation: Store A profit = 0.15 * 15 = Rs. 2.25L. Store B profit = 0.10 * 20 = Rs. 2.0L. Store C profit = 0.12 * 25 = Rs. 3.0L. Store C generated highest profit.

questions.questionText: A line graph tracking inflation rate over 4 quarters: Q1: 4.2%, Q2: 4.8%, Q3: 5.4%, Q4: 5.0%. What is the average quarterly inflation rate?
A stacked bar chart shows energy mix for a country: Renewable (30 GW), Thermal (60 GW), Hydro (20 GW), Nuclear (10 GW). What fraction of total capacity is Renewable?
questions.explanation: Total capacity = 30 + 60 + 20 + 10 = 120 GW. Renewable fraction = 30 / 120 = 1/4 (25%).

questions.questionText: A survey table: 500 households surveyed. Cable TV = 320, Internet = 280, Both = 150. How many households have neither Cable TV nor Internet?
In a pie chart, angles representing expenditures on Food, Rent, Education, and Savings are 144Â°, 90Â°, 72Â°, and 54Â° respectively. If Savings is Rs. 15,000, what is the expenditure on Food?
A bar graph records book sales: Monday: 40, Tuesday: 55, Wednesday: 65, Thursday: 50, Friday: 70, Saturday: 90. What is the average daily sales from Monday to Saturday?
A table records production costs per unit: Material Rs. 45, Labour Rs. 25, Overhead Rs. 10. If selling price is Rs. 100, what is the profit percentage on cost?
A histogram shows test scores of 80 candidates: 0-20 (8), 20-40 (16), 40-60 (28), 60-80 (20), 80-100 (8). What percentage of candidates scored above 60?
questions.explanation: Candidates scoring above 60 = 20 + 8 = 28. Percentage = (28 / 80) * 100% = 35%.

questions.questionText: In a double line graph comparing Revenue and Expenses of a startup over 3 years: Year 1 (Rev: 20L, Exp: 30L), Year 2 (Rev: 45L, Exp: 40L), Year 3 (Rev: 80L, Exp: 55L). What is the cumulative net profit over all 3 years?
questions.explanation: Net year 1 = -10L. Year 2 = +5L. Year 3 = +25L. Cumulative = -10 + 5 + 25 = +20 Lakhs.

questions.questionText: A pie chart shows distribution of 720 students by hobby: Sports 180Â°, Music 90Â°, Reading 60Â°, Drama 30Â°. How many students chose Reading?
questions.explanation: Fraction = 60Â° / 360Â° = 1/6. Students = (1/6) * 720 = 120 students.

questions.questionText: A table records flight delays: On-time (80%), Weather delay (10%), Mechanical (6%), Traffic (4%). Out of 2,500 flights, how many experienced non-weather delays?
questions.explanation: Non-weather delays = Mechanical (6%) + Traffic (4%) = 10%. Flights = 10% of 2500 = 250.

questions.questionText: A bar graph shows branch performance: Branch A (Target: 100, Achieved: 110), Branch B (Target: 120, Achieved: 108), Branch C (Target: 80, Achieved: 92). Which branch had highest percentage target achievement?
A table lists fuel consumption: City driving (12 km/L), Highway (18 km/L). If a driver travels 60 km in city and 180 km on highway, what is the overall average fuel efficiency?
questions.explanation: Fuel in city = 60 / 12 = 5 L. Fuel on highway = 180 / 18 = 10 L. Total distance = 240 km. Total fuel = 15 L. Efficiency = 240 / 15 = 16 km/L.

questions.questionText: In a pie chart, expenditure on sports is 45Â°, culture 90Â°, education 135Â°, and library 90Â°. What fraction of the total budget is allocated to Education?
A table records crop yield (in quintals/hectare): Farm A (yield 40, area 15 ha), Farm B (yield 50, area 25 ha). What is the weighted average crop yield per hectare for both farms combined?
questions.explanation: Total yield = 40 * 15 + 50 * 25 = 600 + 1250 = 1850 quintals. Total area = 40 ha. Average = 1850 / 40 = 46.25 quintals/ha.

questions.questionText: A line graph tracking annual patent filings: 2021: 120, 2022: 150, 2023: 180, 2024: 216. What is the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) multiplier per year?
A bar chart shows quarterly sales (in thousands): Q1: 25, Q2: 35, Q3: 40, Q4: 60. What percent of the total annual sales occurred in the 4th quarter?

In a double bar chart showing male and female literacy rates across 3 districts: District 1 (M: 80%, F: 60%), District 2 (M: 90%, F: 70%), District 3 (M: 85%, F: 75%). Which district has the minimum gender gap in literacy?
questions.explanation: Gaps: District 1 = 20%, District 2 = 20%, District 3 = 10%. District 3 has the minimum gap (10%).

questions.questionText: A table records customer service ratings: Excellent (40%), Good (35%), Average (15%), Poor (10%). If 800 respondents took part, how many rated the service above Average (Excellent or Good)?
questions.explanation: Percentage = 40% + 35% = 75%. Respondents = 0.75 * 800 = 600.

questions.questionText: In a pie chart, angles for marketing channels are: Social Media 126Â°, Search Ads 108Â°, Email 72Â°, Referrals 54Â°. If total marketing budget is Rs. 1,00,000, what is spent on Search Ads?
A table shows employee attrition: Year 1: 12%, Year 2: 15%, Year 3: 10%. If initial staff was 1,000 and 200 new recruits joined at the start of each year, what is the staff count at end of Year 1?
A line graph shows monthly active users (MAU) in thousands: M1: 100, M2: 120, M3: 150, M4: 200. What is the percentage increase in MAU from M1 to M4?
A stacked bar chart indicates revenue sources: Subscriptions (60%), Advertisements (25%), Merchandising (15%). If total revenue is Rs. 20 Crores, find Ad revenue in Crores.
questions.explanation: Ad revenue = 25% of 20 = Rs. 5.0 Crores.

questions.questionText: A table records hospital bed occupancy: Ward A (50 beds, 90% occupied), Ward B (80 beds, 75% occupied), Ward C (70 beds, 80% occupied). What is the overall bed occupancy rate?
questions.explanation: Occupied beds: A = 45, B = 60, C = 56. Total occupied = 161. Total beds = 200. Rate = (161 / 200) * 100% = 80.5%.

questions.questionText: In a pie chart, if the central angle for Rent is 72Â° and Food is 108Â°, what is the ratio of expenditure on Rent to Food?

A bar graph records battery life in hours for 4 phone models: Model A (18 hrs), Model B (24 hrs), Model C (20 hrs), Model D (30 hrs). What is the percentage difference between Model D and Model A relative to Model A?
A table tracks vehicle fuel efficiency: Car 1 (15 km/L), Car 2 (20 km/L). If both cars cover 300 km each, how many total litres of fuel are consumed by both combined?
questions.explanation: Fuel Car 1 = 300 / 15 = 20 L. Fuel Car 2 = 300 / 20 = 15 L. Total fuel = 20 + 15 = 35 litres.

questions.questionText: A histogram showing commute times (in minutes) for 200 workers: 0-15 (40), 15-30 (80), 30-45 (50), 45-60 (30). What percentage of workers commute for 30 minutes or less?
questions.explanation: Workers commuting 30 mins or less = 40 + 80 = 120. Percentage = (120 / 200) * 100% = 60%.

questions.questionText: A double line graph showing quarterly sales of Laptop vs Tablet: Q1 (Lap: 10k, Tab: 15k), Q2 (Lap: 14k, Tab: 16k), Q3 (Lap: 20k, Tab: 18k). In which quarter did Laptop sales first surpass Tablet sales?
questions.explanation: In Q3, Laptop (20k) > Tablet (18k).

questions.questionText: A pie chart shows expenditure on a wedding: Catering 40%, Venue 25%, Decor 15%, Photography 10%, Gifts 10%. If Decor cost Rs. 1,50,000, find the Catering cost.
A table records defect frequencies per 1000 items: Solder defects (15), Component missing (8), Misalignment (7). What is the total non-defective count per 1000 items?
questions.explanation: Total defects = 15 + 8 + 7 = 30. Non-defective = 1000 - 30 = 970.

questions.questionText: A bar graph records solar power generated (in MWh) over 4 days: Day 1: 50, Day 2: 70, Day 3: 65, Day 4: 95. What was the average daily solar generation?
questions.explanation: Total = 50 + 70 + 65 + 95 = 280 MWh. Average = 280 / 4 = 70 MWh.

questions.questionText: A table lists store customer counts: Store 1 (1200), Store 2 (1800), Store 3 (1500). What is Store 2's percentage contribution to total footfall?
A merchant sells an article for Rs. 840 making a profit of 20%. What was the cost price of the article?
A shopkeeper sells two wristwatches for Rs. 1,980 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: When two items are sold at the same selling price, one at x% gain and other at x% loss, there is always an overall loss of (x/10)^2 % = (10/10)^2 % = 1% loss.

questions.questionText: A dishonest grocer uses a false weight of 900 grams instead of 1 kg. If he sells his goods at cost price, find his overall gain percentage.
An article is marked 40% above its cost price. If a discount of 15% is allowed on the marked price, what is the profit percentage earned?
If the cost price of 15 pens is equal to the selling price of 12 pens, what is the gain percentage?
Find the single discount equivalent to a series of successive discounts of 20%, 10%, and 5%.
A man sold an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for Rs. 75 more, he would have gained 20%. What was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Difference in percentage: 20% - (-10%) = 30%. 30% of CP = Rs. 75 => CP = 75 / 0.30 = Rs. 250.

questions.questionText: A manufacturer sells an article to a wholesaler at 10% profit. The wholesaler sells it to a retailer at 20% profit, and the retailer sells it to a customer for Rs. 1,452 at 10% profit. What was the manufacturing cost?
Under a promotional offer of "Buy 4, Get 1 Free", what is the effective discount percentage given to the customer?
questions.explanation: Discount% = [Free Goods / Total Goods Received] * 100% = [1 / (4 + 1)] * 100% = (1/5) * 100% = 20%.
questions.concept: Buy X Get Y Free Equivalence

questions.questionText: A dealer marks his goods 20% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% for cash payment. He also uses a weight of 900 grams for 1 kg. What is his net profit percentage on cash sales?
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1000g = 100. He charges SP for 1000g with markup and discount: 100 * 1.20 * 0.90 = 108. But he only gives 900g whose cost is 90. Profit = 108 - 90 = 18. Profit% = (18 / 90) * 100% = 20%.

questions.questionText: By selling 45 lemons for Rs. 40, a man loses 20%. How many lemons should he sell for Rs. 24 to gain 20% in the transaction?
questions.explanation: SP of 1 lemon = 40/45 = Rs. 8/9. Since he loses 20%, CP of 1 lemon = (8/9) / 0.80 = Rs. 10/9. For 20% gain, required SP of 1 lemon = (10/9) * 1.20 = Rs. 4/3. Number of lemons for Rs. 24 = 24 / (4/3) = 24 * (3/4) = 18 lemons.
questions.concept: Quantity at Target SP and Profit

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells an item at a profit of 25% on the selling price. What is his actual profit percentage on cost price?
questions.explanation: Let SP = 100. Profit = 25. Then CP = 100 - 25 = 75. Actual profit% on CP = (25 / 75) * 100% = 33.33%.

questions.questionText: A milkman buys milk at Rs. 24 per litre. He adds water to it and sells the mixture at Rs. 24 per litre, thereby making a profit of 25%. What is the ratio of water to milk in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Since water is free and mixture is sold at CP, Profit% = (Water / Milk) * 100% = 25% => Water / Milk = 25/100 = 1/4. Ratio of water to milk is 1 : 4.

questions.questionText: A person bought two tables for a total of Rs. 2,000. He sold one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 10%, gaining 5% overall on the whole transaction. Find the cost price of the first table.
questions.explanation: Using Alligation: +20% and -10% mixed to give +5%. Ratio of CP1 : CP2 = [5 - (-10)] : [20 - 5] = 15 : 15 = 1 : 1. Since total CP is Rs. 2000, CP of first table = Rs. 1,000.

questions.questionText: If a book is sold at 10% discount on the marked price, the profit is 20%. What will be the profit percentage if the book is sold at 20% discount on the marked price?
A fruit vendor bought bananas at 6 for Rs. 5 and sold them at 5 for Rs. 6. Find his gain percentage.
A man sells two articles for Rs. 400 each, neither gaining nor losing on the whole. If he sold one at 25% gain, what was the loss percentage on the other article?
questions.explanation: Total SP = 800. Since no overall profit/loss, total CP = 800. First article SP = 400 at 25% gain => CP1 = 400 / 1.25 = Rs. 320. Then CP2 = 800 - 320 = Rs. 480. SP2 = 400. Loss on 2nd = (480 - 400) / 480 = 80 / 480 = 1/6 = 16.67% loss.

questions.questionText: A trader marks up his goods by 50% and then gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is his net profit or loss percentage?
If 10% is lost by selling an article for Rs. 180, at what price must it be sold to gain 20%?
A shopkeeper sells 1/3 of his stock at a profit of 15%, 1/4 at a profit of 20%, and the remaining at a loss of 10%. What is his overall profit percentage on the whole transaction?
A merchant buys an item for Rs. 450 and spends Rs. 50 on transportation. If he sells it for Rs. 600, what is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Total effective CP = 450 + 50 = Rs. 500. SP = Rs. 600. Profit = 600 - 500 = Rs. 100. Profit% = (100 / 500) * 100% = 20%.

questions.questionText: By selling 100 pens, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 20 pens. Find his gain percentage.
questions.concept: Gain Expressed as Units of SP

questions.questionText: A cycle is listed at Rs. 1,500 and a discount of 20% is offered. What additional discount must be offered to bring the net selling price to Rs. 1,104?
questions.explanation: Price after first discount = 1500 * 0.80 = Rs. 1200. Further reduction required = 1200 - 1104 = Rs. 96. Additional discount% = (96 / 1200) * 100% = 8%.

questions.questionText: A trader cheats both his supplier and customer by using false weights to the extent of 10% in buying and selling. What is his total gain percentage?
A dealer sells an article at 6% loss. If he had increased the selling price by Rs. 64, he would have gained 10%. Find the cost price.
If the selling price of an article is 4/3 times its cost price, find the profit percentage.
A retailer buys 30 articles from a wholesaler at the marked price of 27 articles. If he sells them at the marked price, what is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let MP of 1 article = Rs. 1. Total CP for 30 articles = Rs. 27. Total SP for 30 articles = Rs. 30. Profit = 30 - 27 = Rs. 3. Profit% = (3 / 27) * 100% = 11.11%.

questions.questionText: A person sells two cars for Rs. 2,40,000 each. On one he makes a profit of 20% and on the other he suffers a loss of 20%. What is his net financial outcome in rupees?
A shopkeeper offers "Buy 3, Get 2 Free". What is the effective discount percentage?
A shopkeeper sells sugar at a price that recovers the cost of 12 kg by selling 10 kg. What is his profit percentage?
An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 2/3 of this price, there is a loss of 10%. What was the original profit percentage?
questions.explanation: (2/3) SP = 0.90 CP => SP = 0.90 * (3/2) CP = 1.35 CP. Original profit% = 35%.

questions.questionText: A man buys 120 pens at Rs. 3 each. He sells 40 pens at 10% profit and 60 pens at 20% profit. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining pens to earn an overall profit of 15%?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 120 * 3 = Rs. 360. Target total profit = 15% of 360 = Rs. 54. Profit from 40 pens = 40 * 3 * 0.10 = Rs. 12. Profit from 60 pens = 60 * 3 * 0.20 = Rs. 36. Profit needed from remaining 20 pens = 54 - (12 + 36) = Rs. 6. Cost of remaining 20 pens = 20 * 3 = Rs. 60. Required profit% = (6 / 60) * 100% = 10%.

questions.questionText: A cloth merchant marks up cloth by 20% and gives 10% discount, but uses a metre scale which measures only 95 cm. What is his actual gain percentage?
A TV set is sold for Rs. 18,700 with a loss of 15%. At what price should it be sold to gain 15%?
If marked price of an article is Rs. 500 and two successive discounts of 20% and x% reduce the selling price to Rs. 360, find x.
A merchant bought 80 kg of rice at Rs. 13.50/kg and 120 kg at Rs. 16/kg. At what rate per kg should he sell the mixture to gain 20%?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 80 * 13.50 + 120 * 16 = 1080 + 1920 = Rs. 3000. Total weight = 200 kg. Cost per kg = 3000 / 200 = Rs. 15/kg. Target SP with 20% gain = 15 * 1.20 = Rs. 18/kg.

questions.questionText: A reduction of 10% in the price of tea enables a buyer to obtain 250 grams more for Rs. 270. What is the original price per kg of tea?
questions.explanation: Savings = 10% of 270 = Rs. 27. This buys 250g (1/4 kg). Reduced price per kg = 27 / 0.25 = Rs. 108/kg. Original price = 108 / 0.90 = Rs. 120/kg.

questions.questionText: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the same article is sold for Rs. 448. What should be the selling price for making 50% profit?
If an article is sold at 8% gain instead of 8% loss, the seller gets Rs. 28 more. What is the cost price?
A manufacturer marks a watch at Rs. 800. After allowing two successive discounts of 10% and 5% to a retailer, the retailer sells it for Rs. 752.40. What is the retailer's profit percentage?
A person sells an article at 12% profit. If he had bought it for 12% less and sold it for Rs. 9 less, he would have gained 20%. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Let the original cost price be C. The original selling price is 1.12C. The revised cost price is 0.88C, and the revised selling price is 1.12C - 9. A 20% gain means 1.12C - 9 = 1.20(0.88C) = 1.056C. Thus 0.064C = 9, so C = Rs. 140.625.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells an article at 20% profit. If the cost price and selling price both are reduced by Rs. 20, the profit becomes 25%. Find the original cost price.
A dishonest milkman claims to sell his milk at cost price, but he mixes water and gains 16 2/3 %. What is the fraction of water in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Profit = 16 2/3 % = 50/3 % = 1/6. This means for every 6 units of milk, there is 1 unit of water. Total mixture = 6 + 1 = 7 units. Fraction of water in mixture = 1/7.

questions.questionText: An item was sold at a loss of 15%. If it were sold for Rs. 96 more, there would have been a gain of 9%. What is the cost price?
A vendor sells apples at 10 for a rupee, losing 4%. How many apples for a rupee must he sell to gain 20%?
questions.explanation: SP of 10 apples = Rs. 1 => SP of 1 apple = 0.10. CP of 1 apple = 0.10 / 0.96 = 1/9.6. Target SP for 20% gain = (1/9.6) * 1.20 = 1.2 / 9.6 = 1/8. So 8 apples for a rupee.

questions.questionText: Find the single discount equivalent to successive discounts of 30% and 20%.
The marked price of a watch is Rs. 1,600. After two successive discounts, it is sold for Rs. 1,224. If the first discount is 10%, what is the second discount percentage?
questions.explanation: Price after first discount = 1600 * 0.90 = Rs. 1440. Second discount amount = 1440 - 1224 = Rs. 216. Second discount% = (216 / 1440) * 100% = 15%.

questions.questionText: A trader sells two cows for Rs. 19,500 each, one at 20% loss and the other at 15% profit. What is his total profit or loss in rupees?
If cost price of 20 articles is equal to selling price of x articles, and the profit is 25%, find x.
A retailer gets a discount of 40% on the printed price of an article and sells it at the printed price. What is his gain percentage?
questions.explanation: Let Printed Price = 100. CP = 60, SP = 100. Profit = 40. Gain% = (40 / 60) * 100% = 66.67%.

questions.questionText: A merchant incurs a 5% loss by selling a book for Rs. 1140. At what price should he sell it to make a 5% profit?
A dealer bought 200 eggs at Rs. 24 per dozen. 20 eggs were broken. He sold the remaining eggs at Rs. 2.50 each. What was his profit percentage?
An article is sold at a discount of 25% and still makes a profit of 20%. If the cost price is Rs. 1,500, what is the marked price?
questions.concept: Deriving Marked Price from CP and Profit

questions.questionText: A merchant buys two types of rice: Type A at Rs. 30/kg and Type B at Rs. 40/kg in the ratio 3 : 2. If he sells the blend at Rs. 37.40/kg, find his profit percentage.
If profit on selling an article for Rs. 425 is the same as the loss on selling it for Rs. 355, what is the cost price?
A man sold 20 articles for Rs. 60 and gained 20%. How many articles did he buy for Rs. 60?
questions.explanation: SP of 1 article = 60/20 = Rs. 3. CP of 1 article = 3 / 1.20 = Rs. 2.50. Number of articles bought for Rs. 60 = 60 / 2.50 = 24 articles.

questions.questionText: A tradesman marks his goods 30% above CP. If he allows a discount of 6 1/4 %, find his gain percentage.
A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on an item. If the customer paid Rs. 680, what was the marked price?
A manufacturer sells an item for Rs. 3,300, gaining 10%. If the cost of production rises by 12% and he raises his selling price by 10%, what will be his new profit percentage?
Under a scheme of "Buy 5, Get 3 Free", what is the effective discount percentage?
Architect : Blueprint :: Sculptor : ?
